new_identity_gap_counterexample.finding: The v3 binding records expected sibling blob IDs but the filename loader does not verify those bytes before execution. A locally drifted auditor can generate and self-replay evidence under a CLOSE that still claims the frozen auditor blob. Moving the journal to an exact graph catches the mismatch later, but local scientific generation was already under unverified code.

Identity verification must cover the transitive semantic graph, not only the top replay file; otherwise a downstream reporter/auditor can drift under an unchanged top-level binding.

The verified-graph wrapper is fail-closed for ordinary deployment drift, but it is not an adversarial secure loader: a process with write access could race file replacement during a call and restore bytes before the post-check.
A stronger production route should import from immutable content-addressed bytes or an OS/container image whose digest is itself verified, rather than filename paths alone.
